title: Implement Queue using Stacks
statement: Implement Queue operations using two stacks.

testCases.input:
push 1
push 2
pop
push 3
pop
pop

inputOutputContract: Read push x and pop operations, one per line until EOF. pop outputs front value on its own line or -1 if empty.

mistakes.hint1: Inspect the dequeues from input stack behavior in Queue.enqueue / Queue.dequeue; the current algorithm is close, but one operation changes its result.
mistakes.hint2: Start by tracing T1 manually. Watch Queue / s1 / s2 / enqueue / dequeue at each iteration or recursive return.
mistakes.hint3: Check the invariant of Queue.enqueue / Queue.dequeue: Queue.enqueue pushes to s1; dequeue transfers to s2 only when needed and returns FIFO order.
mistakes.hint4: Concentrate on the expression or branch that controls this mistake: `return isEmpty(&queue->s1) ? -1 : pop(&queue->s1);`. What does it do on the failing input?
mistakes.hint5: Compare the intermediate state with the expected output of T1. The mistake is in dequeues from input stack, not merely formatting.
mistakes.hint6: Adjust the faulty operation so that it follows this rule: Queue.enqueue pushes to s1; dequeue transfers to s2 only when needed and returns FIFO order.
mistakes.hint7: A targeted correction is to replace `return isEmpty(&queue->s1) ? -1 : pop(&queue->s1);` with `return isEmpty(&queue->s2) ? -1 : pop(&queue->s2);` in Queue.enqueue / Queue.dequeue, then retest T1–T6.
